approachQuestion.prompt:
Count identifiers that occur exactly twice

Input: an array of integer identifiers. Output: the number of distinct identifiers that appear exactly twice. Example 1: [8, 4, 8, 8, 4, 9] → 1 (only 4 appears exactly twice). Example 2: [5, 5, 5, 5] → 0. Example 3: [] → 0.
constraints: Return one non-negative integer; do not mutate the input.
Assume integer-key hash table lookups and insertions have expected amortized constant cost under an ordinary non-adversarial distribution; this is not a worst-case guarantee.

options.text: Count each identifier in a map, then count the map entries whose frequency is exactly two.
options.feedback: The frequency for each distinct identifier distinguishes exactly two occurrences from one or from three or more.

options.text: Sort a copy of the identifiers, scan each equal-value run, and count runs of length two.
options.feedback: Equal identifiers become adjacent, so every run can be counted correctly. Sorting is removable because a frequency map can accumulate the same counts while scanning.

options.text: For every distinct identifier, scan the whole array to determine its frequency, then count those with frequency two.
options.feedback: This repeatedly scans the input for distinct values. The same exact counts can be accumulated once and then inspected.

options.text: Toggle each identifier in a set: add it when absent and remove it when present; count identifiers left in the set.
options.feedback: Toggling records odd versus even occurrence counts, not exactly two. For [7, 7, 7], 7 remains in the set although its frequency is three.

feedback.reason: The requested result depends on exact multiplicities, so retain enough state to distinguish each frequency.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Count each identifier, then inspect frequencies” shown after your first answer, choose its expected running time and auxiliary-space pair under this explicit model: For this question, assume integer-key hash operations take expected amortized O(1) time under a non-adversarial hash distribution. State expected time on that basis; do not interpret it as an unconditional worst-case guarantee. Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input arrays and the returned scalar/pair, but includes every map/set and temporary structure.
constraints: For this question, assume integer-key hash operations take expected amortized O(1) time under a non-adversarial hash distribution. State expected time on that basis; do not interpret it as an unconditional worst-case guarantee. Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input arrays and the returned scalar/pair, but includes every map/set and temporary structure.

options.text: Expected O(n) time; O(u) auxiliary space, where u is the number of distinct identifiers.
Expected O(n) time; O(1) auxiliary space regardless of the number of distinct identifiers.
O(n log n) time; O(n) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: The input scan builds one count per distinct identifier, and a second pass over those entries checks for frequency two.

details.analyzedMethod: A map stores one integer count for each distinct identifier. After all input values have been processed, the map entries are inspected once.
details.time: Expected O(n + u), which is expected O(n) because u ≤ n. Map lookup/insertion is expected amortized O(1) under the stated hash model.
details.additionalSpace: O(u) map entries. The input and scalar answer are excluded.

q1Alternatives.frequency-map-exactly-two: Correct and the fixed target; all exact frequencies remain available for the final check.
q1Alternatives.sort-and-count-runs: Correct but has removable sorting work: O(n log n) comparison time and O(n) copied values.
q1Alternatives.rescan-for-each-distinct: Correct but inefficient: checking each distinct identifier by a full scan takes O(nu), which is O(n²) when u is proportional to n.
q1Alternatives.toggle-membership-set: Incorrect because parity cannot identify a frequency of exactly two; three occurrences are a counterexample.

q2Options.linear-expected-distinct-space: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hash assumption.
q2Options.linear-constant-space: Incorrect: the map retains counts for up to u distinct identifiers.
q2Options.n-log-n-linear-space: Incorrect for the fixed map method; this describes a sort-based alternative, not its tight expected bound.
q2Options.quadratic-distinct-space: Incorrect for the fixed method; each value and map entry is processed a constant expected number of times.

methodReveal.title: Count each identifier, then inspect frequencies
methodReveal.description: Scan the array and increment the saved count for each identifier. After the scan, visit the saved identifier/count entries and increment the answer only when a count equals two. The answer counts identifiers, not occurrences.
